主要内容: J.C. Penney reported mixed second-quarter results for Q2 2019, with sales declining faster than expected and falling short of analyst forecasts. The company recorded a net loss of $48 million, or 15 cents per share, compared to a loss of $101 million, or 32 cents per share, in the same period the previous year. Excluding one-time items, the loss was 18 cents per share, better than the forecast of 31 cents. However, revenue dropped 7.4% to $2.62 billion, below the expected $2.69 billion. Sales at stores open for at least a year fell 9%, worse than the anticipated 5.2% decline. The company attributed the drop to the discontinuation of appliance and furniture sales. J.C. Penney also announced a partnership with ThredUp, a secondhand retailer, and has been closing stores as part of its restructuring efforts. The company has $1.7 billion in liquidity and aims to maintain at least $1.5 billion for the year. It also reduced inventory by 12.5% and improved its cost of goods sold due to lower permanent markdowns. The retail sector faces challenges as consumers shift to online shopping and direct-to-consumer models. J.C. Penney reported its Q2 2019 earnings, revealing that the company faced delisting risks from the New York Stock Exchange due to its stock price falling below $1. On July 19, its shares dropped below the $1 threshold and continued to trade below that level, hitting an all-time low of 53 cents. However, on Thursday, shares rose more than 8%, trading at around 62 cents. The company stated its intention to increase its share price through improved operating performance or other revenue streams. As of Wednesday's close, shares had declined over 37% since January, resulting in a market value of approximately $181 million. The company has six months to comply with NYSE rules to avoid delisting.
